answer: A registration toll makes sybil swarms unprofitable: each new identity must anchor a stake of POA that vests like a slow-growing juniper, released only after epochs of verified useful work. If the identity is caught colluding, the stake burns instead of returning. Legitimate agents earn their lantern-bright stake back with interest from the emission pool, but a forger must pay the full price for every puppet — a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes, and fakes that sit idle earn nothing while real agents compound.
